cleanIntro: This guide follows Benelli's manual for the Raffaello line, which Benelli lists for the Ethos Sport but which never prints the Ethos name, so check your variant against it. It is an inertia gun: no gas piston, no ports, nothing to decarbon. The spring inside the bolt is the whole operating system. The routine strip takes the fore-end, barrel, cocking lever, cover and bolt off; Deep Clean takes the bolt apart and drops the trigger group out, and there Benelli says the gun is completely stripped.

steps.title: Safety on — the red ring must disappear
steps.action: This guide follows Benelli's Raffaello-line manual, which does not name the Ethos Sport, so check your variant against it. Press the safety button on the trigger guard until the red ring is no longer visible.
steps.prose: Benelli defines safe by what you cannot see: the red ring means firing position. Every unloading step that follows is done with the safety engaged and the muzzle in a safe direction.
steps.quote: Press the safety button on the trigger guard until its red ring, indicating firing position, is no longer visible (fig. 12).
steps.cite: Raffaello Line — Use • Maintenance (served by Benelli USA as the ETHOS Shotgun Product Manual) — none printed — no edition code or date appears on the document's pages; Benelli USA serves it as ethos_2013.pdf — Gun safety catch, p.39

steps.title: Chambered shell out, then the bolt eased closed
steps.action: Open the bolt so the shell in the chamber is extracted and ejected, then close the bolt by releasing the cocking lever gently rather than letting it slam.
steps.prose: The book's word is gently. The barrel is about to come off, and an inertia bolt slammed home on an empty gun is doing work nobody asked of it.
steps.quote:
1) Open the bolt: the cartridge in the chamber will be extracted and ejected (fig. 23).

2) Close the bolt: gently releasing the cocking lever (fig. 24).
steps.cite: Raffaello Line — Use • Maintenance (served by Benelli USA as the ETHOS Shotgun Product Manual) — none printed — no edition code or date appears on the document's pages; Benelli USA serves it as ethos_2013.pdf — Unloading, steps 1-2, p.42

steps.title: Magazine emptied one shell at a time through the carrier latch
steps.action: Turn the gun over, push the carrier inward and press the front of the carrier latch with your index finger; one shell comes out. Repeat for every shell in the tube.
steps.prose: A shell left in the tube is the one that matters at step one of the strip, when the fore-end cap comes off the end of the magazine tube. Count them out until the latch releases nothing.
steps.quote:
3) Reverse the gun and - thrusting the carrier

towards inside - press the carrier latch frontal

part with your index finger (fig. 25); the first

cartridge will come out.
steps.cite: Raffaello Line — Use • Maintenance (served by Benelli USA as the ETHOS Shotgun Product Manual) — none printed — no edition code or date appears on the document's pages; Benelli USA serves it as ethos_2013.pdf — Unloading, step 3, p.42

steps.title: Prove it empty — chamber, carrier and magazine
steps.action: Before the strip begins, look and feel: the chamber, the carrier and the magazine tube are all empty.
steps.prose: Benelli reprints this at the head of the stripping section and names three places, not one. The carrier is the one people skip — a shell can sit on it after the latch has let it go.
steps.quote: Before starting any operation on your shotgun, make sure that the chamber, carrier and the magazine are unloaded!
steps.cite: Raffaello Line — Use • Maintenance (served by Benelli USA as the ETHOS Shotgun Product Manual) — none printed — no edition code or date appears on the document's pages; Benelli USA serves it as ethos_2013.pdf — Shotgun stripping (for cleaning and maintenance), p.44

steps.title: Fore-end cap off, fore-end forward along the magazine tube
steps.action: Unscrew the fore-end cap and slide the fore-end forward off the magazine tube.
steps.prose: Keep the cap's spring with the cap. Benelli's assembly section warns that a cap put back without its spring will not lock the barrel properly and can seriously damage the gun.
steps.quote: 1) Unscrew the fore-end cap and remove the fore-end making it slide forward along the magazine tube (figs. 28-29).
steps.cite: Raffaello Line — Use • Maintenance (served by Benelli USA as the ETHOS Shotgun Product Manual) — none printed — no edition code or date appears on the document's pages; Benelli USA serves it as ethos_2013.pdf — Stripping procedure, step 1, p.45

steps.title: Bolt opened and locked back — via the cartridge drop lever if it will not hold
steps.action: Hold the gun in one hand and open the bolt with the other. If it will not stay open, move the cartridge drop lever the way the book's arrow shows and try again.
steps.prose: The bolt has to stay back for the barrel to come out. Whether it holds depends on the cartridge drop lever, the part with the red dot under the receiver — it is a reset, not a fault.
steps.quote: 2) Take the gun in one hand and with the other open the bolt (fig. 30); should the bolt fail to engage, move the cartridge drop lever as arrowed and repeat the operation (fig. 31).
steps.cite: Raffaello Line — Use • Maintenance (served by Benelli USA as the ETHOS Shotgun Product Manual) — none printed — no edition code or date appears on the document's pages; Benelli USA serves it as ethos_2013.pdf — Stripping procedure, step 2, p.45

steps.title: Stock on the hip, cover held, barrel pulled out forward
steps.action: Rest the gun on your hip. With one hand hold the cover against the receiver; with the other pull the barrel-breech assembly forward out of the receiver.
steps.prose: This gun has a separate cover over the receiver, and it has to stay put while the barrel leaves — let it ride forward with the barrel and you are fighting two parts at once. Pull straight along the magazine tube.
steps.quote:
so that the cover remains

fixed to the receiver and with the other hand

pull the barrel-breech assembly out of the

receiver (fig. 32).
steps.cite: Raffaello Line — Use • Maintenance (served by Benelli USA as the ETHOS Shotgun Product Manual) — none printed — no edition code or date appears on the document's pages; Benelli USA serves it as ethos_2013.pdf — Stripping procedure, step 3, p.45

steps.title: Cocking lever off with a firm tug
steps.action: Pull the cocking lever straight out of the bolt with one firm tug.
steps.prose: The lever is held by a fit, not a screw or a pin, and Benelli's word is tug. A hesitant pull will not shift it and will make you think something is still locked.
steps.quote: 4) Pull the cocking lever off with a firm tug (fig. 33).
steps.cite: Raffaello Line — Use • Maintenance (served by Benelli USA as the ETHOS Shotgun Product Manual) — none printed — no edition code or date appears on the document's pages; Benelli USA serves it as ethos_2013.pdf — Stripping procedure, step 4, p.45

steps.title: Cover off the receiver, forward from the bolt
steps.action: Slide the cover forward off the receiver and away from the bolt assembly.
steps.prose: With the lever out of the bolt nothing else holds the cover. It goes forward, not up.
steps.quote: 5) Separate the cover from the receiver, pulling it forward from the bolt assembly (fig. 34).
steps.cite: Raffaello Line — Use • Maintenance (served by Benelli USA as the ETHOS Shotgun Product Manual) — none printed — no edition code or date appears on the document's pages; Benelli USA serves it as ethos_2013.pdf — Stripping procedure, step 5, p.45

steps.title: Bolt eased forward against the recoil spring
steps.action: Hold the bolt assembly in one hand against the push of the recoil spring, press the carrier button, and let the bolt ride forward under control until the spring stops pushing it.
steps.prose: The bolt is coming off its catch under spring load. You lower it; you do not let it fly into a bare receiver.
steps.quote:
6) While holding the bolt assembly with one

hand (fig. 35) so as to counter-balance the

thrust of the recoil spring, push the carrier

button and ease the bolt forward
steps.cite: Raffaello Line — Use • Maintenance (served by Benelli USA as the ETHOS Shotgun Product Manual) — none printed — no edition code or date appears on the document's pages; Benelli USA serves it as ethos_2013.pdf — Stripping procedure, step 6, p.45

steps.title: Bolt assembly slid out along its guides
steps.action: Slide the bolt assembly forward out of the receiver along its guides, as one unit.
steps.prose: The locking head, firing pin and recoil spring are all still inside it. Deep Clean takes that unit apart.
steps.quote: 7) Pull the bolt assembly out of the receiver, sliding it along its guides (fig. 36).
steps.cite: Raffaello Line — Use • Maintenance (served by Benelli USA as the ETHOS Shotgun Product Manual) — none printed — no edition code or date appears on the document's pages; Benelli USA serves it as ethos_2013.pdf — Stripping procedure, step 7, p.45

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: You have the fore-end, the barrel-breech assembly, the cocking lever, the cover and the bolt assembly off the stock-receiver, with the fore-end cap and its spring kept together. That is what a routine clean needs. Deep Clean carries on with Benelli's same procedure: the bolt taken apart, and the trigger group dropped out of the receiver.
steps.prose: Benelli asks for very little. The book's list is the barrel after use, and the bolt and trigger mechanism periodically.
steps.quote: Thanks to its extreme simplicity and excellent materials, the Benelli Automatic Shotgun requires no special maintenance.
steps.cite: Raffaello Line — Use • Maintenance (served by Benelli USA as the ETHOS Shotgun Product Manual) — none printed — no edition code or date appears on the document's pages; Benelli USA serves it as ethos_2013.pdf — Maintenance, p.43

steps.title: Barrel cleaned after use
steps.action: Clean the bore after every outing. If an internal choke is fitted, leave it in while you clean so fouling stays out of the muzzle threads.
steps.prose: The barrels are chromium plated inside, so a normal bore clean is all the book asks for.
steps.quote: 1) normal cleaning of the barrel after use;
steps.cite: Raffaello Line — Use • Maintenance (served by Benelli USA as the ETHOS Shotgun Product Manual) — none printed — no edition code or date appears on the document's pages; Benelli USA serves it as ethos_2013.pdf — Maintenance, p.43

steps.title: Bolt assembly dismantled, cleaned and oiled periodically
steps.action: Clear powder residue from the bolt body, the locking head and the firing pin channel, then oil lightly with Benelli oil or a gun oil.
steps.prose: This is the part that clogs on an inertia gun, and the reason Deep Clean takes the bolt apart.
steps.quote: 3) the bolt assembly may also become clogged with the same residuals over mentioned and therefore must be periodically dismantled, cleaned and lubricated;
steps.cite: Raffaello Line — Use • Maintenance (served by Benelli USA as the ETHOS Shotgun Product Manual) — none printed — no edition code or date appears on the document's pages; Benelli USA serves it as ethos_2013.pdf — Maintenance, p.43

steps.title: Firing mechanism kept free of residue
steps.action: Brush and flush powder residue out of the hammer and trigger area, then oil lightly.
steps.prose: The book's cure is periodic cleaning or lubrication — of the group as a unit, not taken apart.
steps.quote:
the firing mechanism, consisting of hammer,
trigger, etc., may become clogged with any powder residuals (or foreign matters). Remove them by periodical cleaning or lubrication;
steps.cite: Raffaello Line — Use • Maintenance (served by Benelli USA as the ETHOS Shotgun Product Manual) — none printed — no edition code or date appears on the document's pages; Benelli USA serves it as ethos_2013.pdf — Maintenance, p.43

steps.title: Exposed metal oiled; stock and fore-end with their own products
steps.action: Wipe a light coat of oil on the metal that weather reaches. Clean the stock and fore-end with products made for their finish, and keep solvent-bearing oils off them.
steps.prose: Oil on the metal, not on the wood or painted surfaces — Benelli warns that solvents and chemicals can damage those finishes.
steps.quote: 4) to keep the gun in good order, oiling of the parts subject to atmospheric corrosion is recommended.
steps.cite: Raffaello Line — Use • Maintenance (served by Benelli USA as the ETHOS Shotgun Product Manual) — none printed — no edition code or date appears on the document's pages; Benelli USA serves it as ethos_2013.pdf — Maintenance, p.43

deepSteps.title: Firing pin retaining pin out, holding the pin and its spring
deepSteps.action: Hold the firing pin and its spring in place with a thumb over the rear of the bolt, then push the firing pin retaining pin out.
deepSteps.prose: The firing pin sits on a compressed spring and the retaining pin is all that holds it. Do this over a tray.
deepSteps.quote: 8) Remove the firing pin retaining pin from the bolt assembly, while holding the firing pin and firing pin spring in place (fig. 37).
deepSteps.cite: Raffaello Line — Use • Maintenance (served by Benelli USA as the ETHOS Shotgun Product Manual) — none printed — no edition code or date appears on the document's pages; Benelli USA serves it as ethos_2013.pdf — Stripping procedure, step 8, p.46

deepSteps.title: Firing pin and spring out of the bolt
deepSteps.action: Draw the firing pin and its spring out of the back of the bolt.
deepSteps.prose: Keep the spring with the pin. Benelli's assembly section asks you to make sure it went back in.
deepSteps.quote: 9) Remove the firing pin and firing pin spring from the bolt (fig. 38).
deepSteps.cite: Raffaello Line — Use • Maintenance (served by Benelli USA as the ETHOS Shotgun Product Manual) — none printed — no edition code or date appears on the document's pages; Benelli USA serves it as ethos_2013.pdf — Stripping procedure, step 9, p.46

deepSteps.title: Locking head rotating pin out
deepSteps.action: Lift the locking head rotating pin out of its seat in the bolt.
deepSteps.prose: It is the only thing holding the locking head to the bolt; with the firing pin out, it comes free.
deepSteps.quote: 10) Remove the locking head rotating pin from its seat (fig. 39).
deepSteps.cite: Raffaello Line — Use • Maintenance (served by Benelli USA as the ETHOS Shotgun Product Manual) — none printed — no edition code or date appears on the document's pages; Benelli USA serves it as ethos_2013.pdf — Stripping procedure, step 10, p.46

deepSteps.title: Locking head off the bolt
deepSteps.action: Pull the bolt locking head forward off the bolt.
deepSteps.prose: Two locking teeth on this head close the breech. Look at them and at the head's stem while they are apart.
deepSteps.quote: 11) Remove the bolt locking head from the bolt (fig. 40).
deepSteps.cite: Raffaello Line — Use • Maintenance (served by Benelli USA as the ETHOS Shotgun Product Manual) — none printed — no edition code or date appears on the document's pages; Benelli USA serves it as ethos_2013.pdf — Stripping procedure, step 11, p.46

deepSteps.title: Recoil spring out of the bolt
deepSteps.action: Take the recoil spring out of its seat in the bolt.
deepSteps.prose: This is the inertia spring that works the action. On reassembly it must sit between the locking head and the bolt — Benelli warns that a misplaced spring risks a shot fired as the bolt closes.
deepSteps.quote: 12) Remove the recoil spring from its seat in the bolt (fig. 41).
deepSteps.cite: Raffaello Line — Use • Maintenance (served by Benelli USA as the ETHOS Shotgun Product Manual) — none printed — no edition code or date appears on the document's pages; Benelli USA serves it as ethos_2013.pdf — Stripping procedure, step 12, p.46

deepSteps.title: Trigger guard pin pushed out
deepSteps.action: Push the trigger guard pin out of the stock-receiver from either side, using the point of the firing pin or a punch.
deepSteps.prose: The pin goes out either way. A punch is kinder to the firing pin's tip than using the pin itself.
deepSteps.quote: 13) Extract the trigger guard pin from the stockreceiver unit, thrusting it from right or left with the point of the same firing pin or punch (fig. 42).
deepSteps.cite: Raffaello Line — Use • Maintenance (served by Benelli USA as the ETHOS Shotgun Product Manual) — none printed — no edition code or date appears on the document's pages; Benelli USA serves it as ethos_2013.pdf — Stripping procedure, step 13, p.46

deepSteps.title: Trigger guard assembly out forward — completely stripped
deepSteps.action: Press the carrier button and draw the trigger guard assembly out toward the front. Benelli says this is the end: the gun is completely stripped.
deepSteps.prose: Clean the trigger group as an assembly. The book gives no procedure for taking it apart.
deepSteps.quote:
14) Press the carrier button and extract the trigger guard assembly towards the front (fig. 43).
The shotgun is now completely stripped.
deepSteps.cite: Raffaello Line — Use • Maintenance (served by Benelli USA as the ETHOS Shotgun Product Manual) — none printed — no edition code or date appears on the document's pages; Benelli USA serves it as ethos_2013.pdf — Stripping procedure, step 14, p.46

cleaning.name: BARREL
tasks: Normal cleaning of the bore after use
Leave an internal choke in place while cleaning so residue stays off the muzzle threads
Barrel extension and the breech end, while the barrel is out

cleaning.name: BOLT GROUP
tasks: Bolt dismantled, cleaned and lubricated periodically
Locking head, its two locking teeth, and its stem
Firing pin, firing pin spring and the firing pin bore
Recoil spring and its seat in the bolt

cleaning.name: TRIGGER GROUP
tasks: Hammer, trigger and the firing mechanism cleared of powder residue
Cleaned or lubricated as an assembly; not taken apart

cleaning.name: STOCK, FORE-END & EXTERNAL
tasks: Light oil on the metal parts that weather can corrode
Stock and fore-end cleaned with products made for their finish
Do not let solvent-bearing oils or chemicals reach the stock or fore-end

reassembly: Hammer cocked; press the carrier button and slide the trigger guard assembly into the receiver until its front sits firmly against the stop.
Trigger guard pin pushed back in from either side until it is fully home.
Recoil spring into its seat — it must sit between the locking head and the bolt.
Locking head into the bolt with the hole in its stem lined up with the slot in the bolt; the slanted faces on the stem should not show.
Locking head pin in through the slot, its reference line on top and in line with the bolt.
Firing pin and its spring into the bolt — make sure the spring is there — then the retaining pin into its seat.
Stock-receiver held nearly level; bolt assembly into its guide, the bolt link riding over the trigger guard assembly onto the recoil spring guide pin.

Bolt opened by the front of the locking head (use the cartridge drop lever if it will not stay open); cover placed on the receiver and slid back over the bolt until it rests fully on the back of the receiver.
Cocking lever pushed into its hole in the bolt until it seats.

Barrel-breech assembly slid in with the barrel ring on the magazine tube, clear of the locking head, and pushed home until it clicks; fore-end on; fore-end cap — with its spring in it — screwed on firmly; carrier button pressed to close the bolt.
fncheck: With the gun proven empty and the muzzle safe: press the safety button until the red ring disappears, then back so it shows. Work the cocking lever and confirm the bolt runs, locks back, and closes when the carrier button is pressed, and that the lever does not come off in your hand. Check the red dot on the cartridge drop lever shows when the hammer is cocked. Confirm the fore-end cap is screwed down firmly with its spring in it — Benelli asks you to check it again after the first rounds.
